ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room numbers at a glance
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The key room-stat numbers on one page
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A room is walls and the agreement not to scream in it. These numbers decide how well the agreement holds.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: These are the numbers behind every room panel: what impressiveness is made of, where the labels change, and what a room needs to count as a bedroom, kitchen or hospital. Each one has its own page with what to do about it.

facts.li: Impressiveness = 65 × (average of four factors) + 35 × (smallest factor). The factors are wealth ÷ 1,500, beauty ÷ 3, space ÷ 125, and 1 + (cleanliness ÷ 2.5).
Room mood from impressiveness: under 20 -2 (bedrooms only); 30-39 +1 (bedrooms only); 40-49 +2; 50-64 +3; 65-84 +4; 85-119 +5; 120-169 +6; 170-239 +7; 240 and up +8.
Space is 1.4 per tile, minus 0.9 for every tile under a blocking object. A very impressive bedroom wants about 25 space or more.
Cleanliness of 0.4 or more reads sterile. Sterile tile is +0.6 per tile; filth -5, blood -10, vomit -15.

Room roles: bedroom 100,000; barracks 100,100 per bed; prison cell 170,000; hospital 100,000; kitchen 28 per stove; workshop 27 per bench; lab 60 per item; dining room 12 per table; rec room 7 per item; storeroom 1 per shelf.
Expectations by colony wealth: up to 15,000 +30; to 31,000 +24; to 81,000 +18; to 182,000 +12; to 308,000 +6; above that 0.

advice.li: Click any floor tile and read the room panel: the lowest of the four stats is the one to fix first.
Open the linked pages for what to do about each number.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: impressiveness
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Four room stats make one score, and the weakest one counts double
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A room is only as fine as its worst feature. A gold statue won't fix a floor covered in vomit, and the colony will tell you so at breakfast.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Impressiveness is the single number behind the mood bonus from bedrooms, dining rooms and rec rooms. The game builds it from four stats: wealth, beauty, space and cleanliness. Because the weakest of the four is counted twice in effect, the cheapest way to raise a room is always to fix its lowest stat, not to pile more onto its best one.

facts.li: Each stat becomes a factor: wealth ÷ 1,500, beauty ÷ 3, space ÷ 125, and 1 + (cleanliness ÷ 2.5).
Factors of 1 or more are flattened with a natural log (1 + ln of the factor), so doubling a strong stat adds far less than fixing a weak one.
Impressiveness = 65 × (average of the four factors) + 35 × (the smallest factor).
The result is rounded down to a whole number before the mood table applies.
Very high scores are pulled back by a soft cap, so extreme luxury pays back less and less.

advice.li: Click a tile in the room and compare the four stats on the room panel. Fix the lowest one first.
Go through the cheap fixes in order: a real floor, fewer blocking objects, a sculpture or plant, and a light.
Keep it clean: one blood trail can drop cleanliness into the weakest slot.
Spend on wealth last. A gold statue does nothing for a cramped, dirty room.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: cheap room upgrades
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Floor first, then space, then art, then light: the most mood per log
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Floors first, sculptures second, gold never. That isn't taste, it's arithmetic.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Most rooms can be lifted a whole mood step without spending much. Impressiveness punishes the weakest stat, so the best upgrade is whichever stat is lowest, and that is usually the floor or the space. This is the order veterans follow.

facts.li: A real floor beats soil: soil is -1 cleanliness and -1 beauty on every tile. Smoothed floors and carpet add about +2 beauty; sterile tile gives +0.6 cleanliness.
Every tile you free from blocking furniture gives back 0.9 space.
One sculpture goes a long way: a small sculpture starts at base beauty 50, before material and quality.
Walls count too: smoothed stone +2 beauty, jade +10.
Quality multiplies value, so a skilled artist or builder pays back across every room.
Wooden floors burn with generators on them, so keep power rooms on stone.

advice.li: Lay a floor in every room: wood or stone tile early, carpet or sterile tile later.
Remove furniture that isn't pulling its weight.
Add a sculpture or a plant pot.
Light the room so darkness never sets in: a torch lamp early, a standing lamp once you have power.
Smooth the walls in mountain bases.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room impressiveness mood
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Bedrooms, dining rooms and rec rooms give up to +8 mood when impressive
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: An awful bedroom is a grudge you hand out every night. A wondrous one is a bribe that never runs out.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Colonists get a mood thought from the impressiveness of the bedroom they sleep in and the dining room and rec room they use. The bonus climbs in steps, from nothing in a dull room to +8 in a wondrously impressive one. Only bedrooms can go negative or earn the small "mediocre" bonus.

facts.li: Under 20 (awful): -2, bedrooms only.
20-29 (dull): nothing. 30-39 (mediocre): +1, bedrooms only.
40-49 (decent) +2; 50-64 (slightly impressive) +3; 65-84 (somewhat impressive) +4.
85-119 (very impressive) +5; 120-169 (extremely impressive) +6.
170-239 (unbelievably impressive) +7; 240 and up (wondrously impressive) +8.
Barracks, hospitals and prison cells are also judged by their room stats.

advice.li: Aim for 85 or more in bedrooms: +5 every morning is worth a floor and a sculpture.
Decorate the dining room early. Everyone eats there, so one room lifts the whole colony.
Push rooms just past a step: 84 and 85 differ by a whole mood point, 86 and 119 don't.
Check the Mood tab for "Slept in a ... bedroom" to see which step each colonist is on.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: expectations
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: A poor colony gets +30 mood for free; a rich one gets nothing
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Wealth brings expectations. Expectations bring sulking. Sulking brings fire.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Every colonist gets a flat mood bonus that depends on how wealthy the whole colony is. A young, poor colony enjoys +30 that quietly shrinks as wealth grows, so the comforts that kept people happy at the start stop being enough. Plan rooms, food and recreation to grow along with your wealth.

facts.li: Growing from 30,000 to 100,000 wealth takes every colonist from +24 to +12.
Royalty and Ideology add higher tiers (Noble, Royal, Elite, Supreme) worth -6 or -12.
Conceited nobles start at moderate and climb one level per title: -6 at Baron, -12 at Archon or above.
Higher expectations also want more kinds of recreation: 2 at extremely low, up to 6 at sky-high. Slaves have expectations of their own.

advice.li: Watch the "Expectations" line in the Mood tab; a mood slump right after wealth crosses a boundary is this.
Before a big trade or loot haul, make sure rooms and meals can carry the drop.
Don't hoard silver and materials you'll never use: they raise wealth without making anyone happier.
Move from barracks to private rooms, and from simple to fine meals, as wealth climbs.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room space
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Space is 1.4 per tile, and every blocking piece of furniture eats into it
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A three-by-three bedroom is a closet with ambitions. Give folk room to turn around without kneeing the dresser.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Space measures how roomy a room feels, and it's one of the four parts of impressiveness. Each tile adds space, but every tile covered by a bed, table or shelf takes most of that back, so the same room can feel fine empty and cramped once furnished. Chairs and stools don't count against it.

facts.li: Space = 1.4 per tile. Each tile under a blocking object takes away 0.9, so a furnished tile is worth 0.5.
Labels: under 12.5 cramped; 12.5-28.9 rather tight; 29-54.9 average-sized; 55-69.9 somewhat spacious; 70-129.9 quite spacious; 130-349.4 very spacious; 349.5 and up extremely spacious.
An empty 5x5 room has 35 space. Add a bed, table, light, heater, plant pot and artwork and it drops to 27.8.
Rough sizes once furnished: 3x4 or smaller is cramped; 3x6 or 4x5 rather tight; 4x7 or 5x6 average.
A very impressive bedroom wants about 25 space or more: a furnished 5x5 or 4x6 works, a 4x4 is a struggle.
A room can span at most 36 map regions, up to 5,184 tiles (72x72). An empty 50x50 is the largest that avoids region trouble.

advice.li: Build bedrooms 5x5 inside, or 4x6, if you want them to reach "very impressive".
Don't fill rooms with furniture that isn't working: every blocking tile costs 0.9 space.
Use chairs and stools freely; they don't reduce space.
When wood is short, build one big barracks or dining hall instead of several small rooms.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room cleanliness
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Cleanliness is the average of every tile, and one blood trail goes a long way
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Never mind what caused the fever. Wash the floor.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: A room's cleanliness is the average of every tile in it: the floor itself plus any filth lying on it. It feeds impressiveness, and in kitchens and hospitals it also decides food poisoning, infections and surgery success. A good floor gives you a head start; regular cleaning keeps it.

facts.li: Labels: under -1.1 very dirty; -1.1 to -0.41 dirty; -0.4 to -0.06 slightly dirty; -0.05 to 0.39 clean; 0.4 and up sterile.
Floors: sterile tile +0.6; steel, silver or gold +0.2; most built floors and natural stone 0; straw matting -0.1; soil and gravel -1; mud, marsh, broken asphalt and chunks -2.
Filth on a tile: dirt, rubble and other filth -5; blood -10; vomit, insect blood and fuel -15; corpse bile -20.
For impressiveness, cleanliness 0.6 gives a factor of about 1.24, and -1 gives about 0.6.
A dirty kitchen raises food poisoning; a dirty hospital raises infection chance and lowers surgery success.

advice.li: Floor every room you care about. Soil counts -1 on every tile, forever.
Use sterile tile in the hospital and kitchen once you can, and stone or wood tile elsewhere.
Make sure someone has Cleaning enabled and that your rooms sit inside the home area.
Keep butchering out of the kitchen and bodies out of the base: blood is -10 on every tile it touches.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: beauty
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What makes a room pretty: floors, walls, art, and no blood on the floor
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Sweep the floor, haul the rubble, stick a plant pot by the door. It's cheaper than a funeral.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Beauty is how nice a place looks, and it counts twice: once in room impressiveness and once in each colonist's Beauty need. A pawn takes in the tiles around it that walls don't hide, so a pretty room helps everyone working or eating inside. Filth and bare ground drag it down fast; art, good floors and smoothed walls lift it.

facts.li: A pawn feels the average beauty of the tiles it can see within 8 tiles (up to 241 tiles); walls and doors shrink that area.
Floor tiles: bare rough stone or soil -1, a dirty tile -5, blood -30, vomit -40. Smoothed floors and carpets raise the average by about 2.
Walls: smoothed +2, marble +1, jade +10.

Art is (base × material modifier + material offset) × quality. Small sculpture base 50, large 100, grand 400; good quality ×2, legendary ×8. A good marble small sculpture is (50 × 1.35 + 1) × 2 = 137; a legendary gold grand one reaches 12,960.
Room labels: under -3.5 hideous; -3.5 to 0 ugly; 0-2.39 neutral; 2.4-4.9 pretty; 5-14.9 beautiful; 15-49.9 very beautiful; 50-99.9 extremely beautiful; 100 and up unbelievably beautiful.
Small rooms are penalized: a room of 40 tiles or less counts as 20 + half its size when its beauty is averaged.

advice.li: Lay a real floor before buying art; bare soil and rough stone cost -1 on every tile.
Put one high-quality sculpture in the middle of a big room rather than many cheap pieces in corners.
Move loose items onto shelves; stacks lying on the floor are ugly.
Smooth the stone walls in mountain bases.
Give art jobs to your best artist: quality multiplies beauty.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: light and darkness
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Light every room: darkness costs mood, spoils surgery and invites bugs
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Dark rooms breed insects and opinions. Light a lamp and you'll have fewer of both.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Colonists who spend long stretches awake in the dark get an unhappy thought, and it wears their mood down. Light also matters for surgery, and insect hives prefer dark corners. A light in every room is one of the cheapest fixes in the game.

facts.li: Colonists awake in a dark place get an "In darkness" mood penalty; light every room rather than cutting it fine.
Surgery suffers when the head of the bed sits under 50% light, down to ×0.75 success in total darkness.
Infestations favor dark spots.
Torch lamps burn wood and need refueling; standing lamps and sun lamps need power.

advice.li: Put a light in every bedroom, workshop, kitchen, hospital and corridor.
Early or tribal: torch lamps, kept off wooden floors and away from wooden walls. Later: standing lamps.
Place the hospital's light near the head of the beds.
Light the far corners of mountain bases; the bugs like the dark.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room wealth
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The value of what's inside: easy to raise, wasted if another stat is lowest
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A golden bed in a dirt hole is still a dirt hole. The raiders will want it more, mind.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Room wealth is simply the market value of everything in the room. It's the easiest of the four impressiveness stats to raise, since one or two valuable pieces can do it, but it's wasted while space or cleanliness is the weakest factor. Everything you add also counts toward the colony wealth that raids and expectations follow.

facts.li: Labels: under 500 impoverished; 500-699 somewhat poor; 700-1,999 mediocre; 2,000-3,999 somewhat rich; 4,000-9,999 rich.
10,000-39,999 luxurious; 40,000-99,999 very luxurious; 100,000-999,999 extremely luxurious; 1,000,000 and up unbelievably luxurious.
The wealth factor is wealth ÷ 1,500, so about 1,500 silver of contents gives a factor of 1.0.
A bedroom with nothing but a bed reads "impoverished".

advice.li: Raise wealth last, after the floor, space and cleanliness.
Buy or make a few good-quality pieces rather than a pile of cheap ones.
Remember every silver of room wealth also raises colony wealth, and with it your expectations and the next raid.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: room roles
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: How the game decides what a room is, and why a bed beats a stove
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Put a bed in the kitchen and you don't have a kitchen. You have a bedroom that smells of onions.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Every room gets one role, like bedroom, kitchen or hospital, and the role decides which room thoughts and bonuses apply. The game scores each possible role from the furniture inside and picks the highest. Beds score so high that any room with one becomes a bedroom or barracks, whatever else is in it.

facts.li: Bedroom 100,000 if valid; barracks 100,100 per ordinary bed; hospital 100,000 (needs a medical bed).
Prison cell 170,000 (one prisoner bed); prison barracks 100,100 per prisoner bed.
Kitchen 28 per cooking station; workshop 27 per workbench (crafting spots don't count); laboratory 60 per lab item.
Dining room 12 per table; rec room 7 per recreation item; storeroom 1 per shelf.
The highest score wins; a tie goes to the role checked first.
A room with a bed and a stove is a bedroom or barracks, not a kitchen: 100,000 beats 28.

advice.li: Give each job its own room, so every bonus keeps working.
Check the header of the room panel. If it just says "Room", the game didn't recognize what you built.
Keep beds out of kitchens, workshops and dining rooms.
DLC rooms such as throne rooms, temples and nurseries have their own rules; check their header too.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: bedrooms and sleep
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: What makes a valid bedroom, and the bad nights that cost -4 each
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A bed is a treaty with the night. Sleep on the ground and the night sends you the bill in the morning.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: A private bedroom is the cheapest lasting mood bonus in the game, but only if the game counts it as a bedroom. A medical bed, a spare bed or the wrong roommate turns it into something else. Sleeping rough has its own costs: each bad night leaves a -4 thought for a day.

facts.li: A room is not a bedroom if it has no ordinary bed, has a medical or prisoner bed, has more than one unassigned bed, or the people assigned to it aren't partners.
A room with a child assigned only counts as a bedroom if a parent is assigned too.
Bad nights, each lasting 1 day: slept on the ground -4, slept outside -4, slept in the cold -4, slept in the heat -4, disturbed sleep -1.
An awful bedroom (impressiveness under 20) costs -2; a very impressive one (85 or more) gives +5.
A 4x2 room has only about 11 space and reads cramped; very impressive bedrooms want about 25.

advice.li: Give each colonist a room of about 5x5 with a real floor, a light, a dresser or end table and a plant or sculpture.
Keep bedrooms walled, roofed and heated or cooled, so nobody sleeps in the cold or heat.
Keep corridors out of bedrooms so nobody walks past sleepers.
Tribal: a bedroll in a small roofed hut with a torch lamp beats any bed in the open.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: barracks or bedrooms
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: One shared room is cheap; private rooms let people sleep in peace
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Barracks are fine until someone snores, someone sleepwalks, and someone else owns a pistol.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: A barracks is any room with two or more ordinary beds that isn't a valid bedroom. Everyone sleeping there shares one impressiveness score, so one big, clean, decorated barracks can match several private rooms for the price of one set of decor. The catch is that sleepers disturb each other, and experienced players move people into private rooms as soon as they can.

facts.li: A barracks scores 100,100 per ordinary bed, and nothing if the room holds a prisoner bed or is a valid bedroom.
All sleepers share one impressiveness score and get the room thought from it.
People walking past sleepers cause "Disturbed sleep": -1 for a day.
Veterans find shared quarters a steady mood drag, with sleepers disturbing each other, and move people to private rooms early.

advice.li: Use a barracks for the first weeks, and for soldiers and new arrivals.
Keep it off the main corridors so nobody walks through while others sleep.
Decorate it like one big bedroom: one sculpture and one good floor serve every sleeper.
Build private rooms as soon as wood and space allow; as wealth and expectations grow, the barracks hurts more.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: eating at a table
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Eating without a table costs -3; a fine dining room gives up to +8
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Eating standing up is how muffalo do it. We're not muffalo. Build a table.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Colonists want a table to eat at, and they're unhappy when they can't find one. A room becomes a dining room through its tables, and it's one of the three rooms whose impressiveness gives a mood bonus. Since everyone eats there every day, a clean, decorated dining room pays off faster than almost anything else.

facts.li: Ate without table: -3 for 1 day.
A dining room scores 12 per table; 1x2, 2x2, 2x4 and 3x3 tables all count.
A decorated dining room gives up to +8 from impressiveness; a bare, dull one gives nothing.
Meal moods stack on top: raw food -7, nutrient paste -4, fine meal +5, lavish meal +12.

advice.li: Build the dining room right next to the kitchen so meals don't travel across the base.
Keep it away from the butcher room and the corpse pile.
Add a small table near far-off fields or mines; colonists only walk so far to eat.
Use chairs and stools generously: they don't cost space.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: recreation buildings
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: How much fun each game, TV and instrument gives, and how many can use it
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Joy is scheduled because happiness, left alone, wanders off.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Recreation buildings refill your colonists' Recreation need, and a room full of them becomes a rec room with its own impressiveness bonus. Each building has a number of spots for users and a multiplier on how fast it gives joy. Variety matters more than one perfect building, because colonists get bored of doing the same thing.

facts.li: A rec room scores 7 per recreation item.
Base gain is 36% per hour × the building's multiplier, before tolerance.
Horseshoes pin and hoopstone ring: 12 spots, 100%. Chess table: 4 spots (2 users), 100%. Game of Ur: 4 (2), 80%.
Billiards table: 2 spots, 130% (about 46.8% an hour). Poker table: 8 (4), 130%. Telescope: 1, 120%.
Tube TV: 15 spots, 120%. Flatscreen TV: 30, 140% (about 50.4% an hour). Megascreen TV: 42, 160%.
Harp, harpsichord and piano: 1 each, 100%, for music.

advice.li: Mix kinds: a game table, horseshoes, a TV and an instrument beat four of the same.
Put a TV in the hospital: bedridden patients can only watch TV.
Without power, skip the TVs; the games, the telescope and the instruments need none.
Put the rec room between the bedrooms and the dining room so people pass it every day.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: hospital and prison rooms
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Hospitals need medical beds; a cell is built around one prisoner bed
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: A prisoner and a colonist differ mostly in paperwork and in which door they're allowed through.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Hospitals and prison cells are rooms like any other, and the game recognizes them by their beds. A hospital needs at least one medical bed and no prisoner bed; a cell is built around prisoner beds and nothing else. Both deserve care: a clean, lit hospital saves lives, and a decent cell keeps prisoners calm.

facts.li: A hospital scores 100,000. A prisoner bed in it, or no medical bed at all, breaks it.
A prison cell holds one prisoner bed and scores 170,000. An ordinary colonist bed breaks it.
More prisoner beds make a prison barracks: 100,100 per bed, 50,001 per medical prisoner bed.
A prisoner's mood uses the cell's impressiveness, as a bedroom does.
Colonists and slaves can't share a room with prisoners.
Surgery suffers when the head of the bed is under 50% light, down to ×0.75 in full darkness.

advice.li: Keep the hospital clean, lit and floored, with sterile tile once you can.
Don't build cramped cells; prisoners feel it.
Set beds to "medical" or "for prisoners" after building them, or the room won't count.
Put a TV in the hospital so bedridden patients have some recreation.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: mood numbers at a glance
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: The key mood numbers on one page
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Sleep in a bed. Eat at a table. Die in a hospital. That's civilization.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: These are the thoughts and thresholds you'll check most when a colonist's mood bar turns red. Each number has its own page with what to do about it.

facts.li: Mental breaks: minor below 35% mood, major below 20%, extreme below 5%. Average time to a break: 4, 0.8 and 0.5 days.
Room impressiveness: up to +8; an awful bedroom -2.
Sleep: on the ground, outside, in the cold or in the heat -4 each; disturbed -1.
Food: raw -7, nutrient paste -4, fine meal +5, lavish meal +12, no table -3.
Recreation: +10 near full, -20 when empty. Beauty need: +15 to -15.
Corpses: observed -4, rotting -6, for half a day. Catharsis after a break: +40 per stack, 122 at most, for 3 days.

advice.li: Find the biggest negative thought in the Mood tab and fix that first.
Open the linked page for each number to see what to do about it.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: mental breaks
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Below 35% mood breaks can start; below 5% they turn deadly
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Mood is a ledger. The bill arrives at the worst possible hour, usually holding a lit torch.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: When a colonist's mood stays below a break threshold, they can snap and stop taking orders. Minor breaks waste time, major ones break things, and extreme ones can kill someone or burn down the base. A break ends with a burst of relief called catharsis, but if you're relying on it, mood is too low somewhere else.

facts.li: Thresholds: minor 35% mood ("Stressed"), major 20% ("On edge"), extreme 5% ("About to break"). Traits move the minor threshold, within 1% to 50%.
Average time to a break while below a threshold: minor 4 days, major 0.8 days, extreme 0.5 days.
Minor: food binge, sad wander, hiding in a room, insulting spree, crying, giggling, dark visions.
Major: social drug binge, daze, tantrum, bedroom tantrum, sadistic rage, corpse obsession, insane ramblings.
Extreme: berserk, fire-starting spree, hard drug binge, catatonic breakdown, jailbreaker, slaughterer, murderous rage, run wild, giving up and leaving.
Catharsis after a break: +40 per stack, up to 5 stacks with a 0.75 multiplier (122 at most), for 3 days.
Void catharsis (Anomaly): 30 per stack, up to 5 stacks (150 at most), for 3 days.

advice.li: Watch the three marks on each mood bar, and act when someone drifts toward 35%.
Quick fixes: a batch of fine meals, a recreation block in the schedule, a beer, or a day off from hard jobs.
Remove the sources of bad thoughts: corpses, ugly corridors, sleeping on the floor.
Set drug policies so a binge finds nothing hard to binge on.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: beauty need
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Pretty surroundings give up to +15 mood; ugly ones cost up to -15
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Nobody notices a pretty bedroom while they're asleep. Everybody notices the blood in the corridor on the way to breakfast.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Each colonist has a Surroundings need that fills when they spend time somewhere beautiful and drains somewhere ugly. It's one of the biggest mood swings you control directly, from +15 to -15. Sleeping colonists barely notice their bedroom's looks, so the beauty that matters is where people are awake: workshops, the dining room, the hospital and the main corridors.

facts.li: Beauty 6 or more fills the need: +15.
4.5 or more: +10. 2.5 or more: +5.
From -0.5 up to 2.5: no thought.
-3.5 or more: -5. Below that -10, and -15 once it reaches -4.
Short trips through ugly places matter little: the need rises faster than it falls.
Extra beauty in a bedroom barely affects a sleeping colonist's mood.

advice.li: Spend beauty where people stay awake: the workshop, dining room, rec room, hospital and main walkways.
After a raid, mop the corridors first: blood is -30 and vomit -40 beauty per tile.
Put stockpiles on shelves; loose items on the floor count as ugly.
Place one good sculpture in the middle of a big room rather than several small ones in the corners.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: recreation and boredom
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Recreation swings mood from +10 to -20, and one game alone gets boring
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Chess every night gets old. Give them three ways to waste time, or they'll invent a fourth, and it'll involve fire.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Recreation is a need that drains while colonists work and refills when they play, chat or relax. Each kind of fun builds tolerance as it's used, so a colonist who only plays chess gets bored of it and gains less. The richer the colony, the more different kinds of fun people expect.

facts.li: Recreation falls 2.5% per hour above 30%, 1.75% per hour at 15-30% and 1% per hour below 15%. It doesn't fall while sleeping, having fun or in a mental break.
Tolerance builds at two-thirds of the recreation gained. Above 50% tolerance a colonist is bored of that kind until it drops below 30%.
Tolerance lost per day, and kinds of recreation wanted, by expectations: extremely low 18% / 2; very low 13% / 3; low 11% / 3; moderate 10% / 4; high 8% / 5; sky-high 7% / 6.
Slaves and prisoners have no Recreation need.

advice.li: Offer at least as many kinds of recreation as your expectation level asks for, and add more as wealth grows.
Give everyone a recreation hour or two in the schedule so they actually use it.
Count chatting, meditation, cloud watching, viewing art and drinks as kinds too.
Tribal: horseshoes, a chessboard, an instrument and a barrel of beer cover several kinds without power.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: temperature comfort
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Keep rooms around 16-26 °C: outside that people sulk, slow down and get sick
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Too warm and tempers rise; too cold and toes start leaving. Find the middle and shut the door.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Every colonist has a comfortable temperature range that their clothes move up or down. Outside it they feel hot or cold, sleep badly, and in the worst cases fall to heatstroke or hypothermia. Workbenches have a comfortable range too, so a freezing workshop slows the whole colony.

facts.li: Each pawn has a minimum and maximum comfortable temperature; apparel shifts both.
About 16-26 °C indoors is a common target.
Sleeping in the cold or in the heat: -4 for a day.
Many benches, such as the electric stove and stonecutter's table, are comfortable at 10-35 °C and work at 70% speed outside it.
Heat waves add up to 17 °C; cold snaps take away 20 °C.
Creatures take burn damage 150 °C beyond their comfortable range, and no animal is comfortable above 60 °C.

advice.li: Heat bedrooms and workshops in winter and cool them in summer. Industrial: heaters and coolers. Tribal: a campfire for heat and passive coolers for summer.
Close doors and finish walls and roofs; heaters and coolers only hold a closed room.
Give outdoor workers jackets, dusters or parkas for the season.
Remember passive coolers can't go below 17 °C: enough to stop heatstroke, never enough for food.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: corpses and filth
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Bodies cost -4 to -6 mood on sight; blood and vomit wreck rooms
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: If you can smell the corpse pile from the dining hall, it's in the wrong place.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Colonists hate seeing bodies, and they hate rotting ones more. After a raid, the corpses and blood left in the corridors drag down mood, beauty and cleanliness all at once. Hauling the dead away and mopping up quickly is part of winning the fight.

facts.li: Observed corpse: -4. Observed rotting corpse: -6. Each lasts half a day.
Blood: -10 cleanliness and -30 beauty per tile. Vomit: -15 and -40. Other filth: -5 and -5.
A butcher table in the kitchen puts blood where the food is made and raises food poisoning risk.

advice.li: Haul bodies to a dump zone or graves well away from where people walk, eat and sleep.
Bury your own dead in a grave or crypt.
After a raid, give a low-skill colonist a high Cleaning priority to mop the corridors.
Keep butchering in its own room, away from the kitchen and dining room.

ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.label: cabin fever
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.summary: Colonists who never see the sky get restless; give them time outside
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.tip: Researchers who never see the sky start talking to the bench. Send them out to throw horseshoes.
ColonyCouncil.AlmanacArticleDef.description: Colonists like some time under the open sky. Spending every hour under a roof, especially in a mountain base, builds up an indoors mood penalty. A little time outside each day is cheap insurance.

facts.li: Colonists who spend all their time under a roof risk an indoors mood penalty that grows the longer it lasts.
Mountain bases, where every room sits under rock, are the most at risk.
Crafters, researchers and cooks stay under a roof all day; farmers and haulers get out without trying.
Walking through puddles makes colonists wet, with a small mood hit each time.

advice.li: Leave an unroofed courtyard or garden inside your walls.
Put horseshoes or a hoopstone ring outside, so recreation happens under the sky.
Mix an outdoor job, like hauling or plant cutting, into the day of your indoor workers.
Give everyone some "Anything" hours in the schedule.
